# 01 geo index -- Elasticsearch geo query DSL -> Doris SQL (plan 01 Z.1, Goal G2)

Doris side = this fork (bartuer/doris `geo-index`): `s2_cell` + an inverted index on a generated column, with
`ST_Contains` rewritten to use it automatically (plan 01 Phase C; fix.archive/01.geo.index.reuse.md).

## 1. Mapping / DDL

| Elasticsearch | Doris |
|---|---|
| `"location": {"type": "geo_point"}` | two columns `lon DOUBLE, lat DOUBLE` (Doris has no point column type for storage; `ST_Point(lon, lat)` builds one in queries) |
| the BKD index ES builds for every `geo_point` | `geo_cell BIGINT AS (s2_cell(lat, lon))` + `INDEX idx_geo (geo_cell) USING INVERTED` |
| `geo_shape` field (polygons, lines stored per document) | not covered: this index is for points (plan 01 G1) |

```sql
CREATE TABLE places (
  id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  name VARCHAR(128),
  lon DOUBLE NOT NULL,
  lat DOUBLE NOT NULL,
  geo_cell BIGINT AS (s2_cell(lat, lon)),       -- argument order: lat, lon
  INDEX idx_geo (geo_cell) USING INVERTED
) DUPLICATE KEY(id) DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(id) BUCKETS 16;
```
Rules the planner checks before using the index (`GeoIndexRewrite`): the column must be BIGINT, generated
exactly as the 2-argument `s2_cell(<lat col>, <lon col>)` (level 16), and have an inverted index.

## 2. Queries

| ES query DSL | Doris SQL | index used |
|---|---|---|
| `geo_shape` `{"shape": {"type": "polygon", "coordinates": [[[lon,lat], ...]]}, "relation": "within"}` on a `geo_point` | `WHERE ST_Contains(ST_Polygon('POLYGON((lon lat, ...))'), ST_Point(lon, lat))` | yes (rewritten to `s2_covers(geo_cell, ...) AND ST_Contains(...)`) |
| `geo_shape` `relation: "intersects"` with a polygon, on a `geo_point` | same as `within` (for a point, intersects == within, up to boundary points, see 3.3) | yes |
| `geo_polygon` `{"points": [{"lat":..,"lon":..}, ...]}` (deprecated 7.12) | same as `within`; write the points as `lon lat` and repeat the first point at the end | yes |
| `geo_shape` with WKT `"shape": "POLYGON ((lon lat, ...))"` | `ST_Polygon('POLYGON((lon lat, ...))')` -- WKT is copied as is | yes |
| polygon with holes (GeoJSON rings 2..n / WKT inner rings) | WKT with inner rings: `POLYGON((outer), (hole), ...)` | yes |
| `geo_shape` `"type": "envelope", "coordinates": [[minLon, maxLat], [maxLon, minLat]]` | `ST_Polygon('POLYGON((minLon minLat, maxLon minLat, maxLon maxLat, minLon maxLat, minLon minLat))')` | yes |
| `geo_bounding_box` | `lon BETWEEN minLon AND maxLon AND lat BETWEEN minLat AND maxLat` (a true lat/lon box is what ES means) | no (plain column filters; the s2 index is for polygons) |
| `geo_distance` `{"distance": "2km", "location": [lon, lat]}` | `ST_Distance_Sphere(lon, lat, <lon0>, <lat0>) <= 2000` | no (not in plan 01 scope) |
| `relation: "disjoint"` | `NOT ST_Contains(...)` | no (a negation cannot use a superset index) |
| `relation: "contains"` on a `geo_point` | only true for a degenerate point query shape; not mapped | -- |

## 3. Differences that change results

### 3.1 Coordinate order
GeoJSON / ES arrays are `[lon, lat]`, and WKT is `lon lat` in both systems.  `ST_Point(lon, lat)` takes lon
first, `s2_cell(lat, lon)` takes lat first (same order as `h3_lat_lng_to_cell`).  ES `geo_polygon` objects
`{"lat":..,"lon":..}` and strings `"lat,lon"` must be swapped when written into WKT.

### 3.2 Ring closure and orientation
WKT rings are closed (first point repeated at the end); ES GeoJSON polygons must be closed too, and
`geo_polygon` points are closed implicitly.  Orientation: Doris normalises a loop to the smaller of its two
regions (S2 `Normalize`, at most a hemisphere).  ES uses the `orientation` mapping parameter (default
right-hand / counter-clockwise).  Polygons smaller than a hemisphere behave the same either way.

### 3.3 Edges: planar (ES) vs geodesic (Doris) -- the main semantic difference
ES "predicates are evaluated using Apache Lucene's 2D geo implementation ... not great-circle or geodesic"
(ES geo_shape docs, "Semantics").  Doris `ST_Contains` is S2: polygon edges are great-circle arcs.  An edge
of constant latitude therefore bulges poleward in Doris.  Measured / computed:

| edge | geodesic bulge vs the planar edge |
|---|---|
| plan 01 "city" top edge, lat 40.05, 35 km | 14.7 m -- 83 of 273,872 points (0.03%) lie between the two (MEASURED on the B.2 10 M dataset: hits with lat > 40.05) |
| 110 km east-west edge at 10 N | 41.5 m |
| 300 km east-west edge at 40 N | 1.08 km |
| 550 km east-west edge at 60 N | 10.5 km |

Consequences:
- An ES user migrating city-scale polygons sees at most tens of metres of difference along long east-west
  edges.  For continent-scale polygons, densify the edges (insert points every ~10 km) before sending
  them to either system, so both converge to the same boundary.
- Boundary points: ES WITHIN includes points on the boundary; Doris `GeoPolygon::contains` excludes points
  lying exactly on an edge (`point_on_edge`, 02.audit.design.md #3).  Only exact boundary points can differ.
- The Doris index never changes Doris results: `s2_covers` is a superset of the geodesic polygon, and
  `ST_Contains` rechecks exactly (G3: hits identical to the unindexed query, 3 polygons x 10 M rows).

### 3.4 Antimeridian
ES GeoJSON polygons crossing +-180 must be split or use `orientation`.  Doris WKT may cross the antimeridian
directly (S2 is on the sphere): `POLYGON((179 -17, -179 -17, -179 -15, 179 -15, 179 -17))` is a 2-degree box
across it (plan 02 fixture `antimeridian`).

### 3.5 Precision
ES quantises stored points to ~1 cm (encoded lat/lon ints).  Doris stores DOUBLE lon/lat; `s2_cell` uses
level-16 cells (~150 m) only for the index, and the recheck uses the full-precision DOUBLEs.

## 4. Checked on the cluster (2026-11-19T21:30Z, 10 M rows, plan 01 B.2 data)

Same SQL on `geo_pts_idx` (indexed, rewritten) and `geo_pts` (no cell column):

| ES shape | Doris WKT | indexed hits | unindexed hits | rewritten |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| envelope [[116.3, 40.0], [116.5, 39.8]] | `POLYGON((116.3 39.8, 116.5 39.8, 116.5 40.0, 116.3 40.0, 116.3 39.8))` | 90,961 | 90,961 | yes |
| polygon with hole | `POLYGON((116.2 39.75, ... ), (116.3 39.85, ... ))` | 205,144 | 205,144 | yes |
| across the antimeridian | `POLYGON((179 -17, -179 -17, -179 -15, 179 -15, 179 -17))` | 125 | 125 | yes |
